records.region: Eastern Falcón; southwestern inland approach to the Hueque estuary and Caribbean coast
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen southwestern opening, long upper/middle corridor, meaningful tributary joins and transition into the lower mapped estuary lack ordinary corridor-scale source correspondence. Named-basin and tributary prose cannot replace those geographic through-links.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The lower western estuarine branch and Caribbean outlet are supported. The whole selected southwestern-to-coastal route is not established; Río Hueque is not assigned as a uniform name to every selected upstream part.
records.completion_scope: Bounded pass completed with primary-source support for lower Hueque estuarine identity and actual Caribbean terminal, while explicitly retaining the long inland through-link gaps.
records.supported_name_scope: The local estuary study identifies Río Hueque and distinguishes Río Curarí. FEP regional prose names Upipe, Remedios/Los Remedios, Jacura and Guamure as basin context without fixing their boundaries on the selected route.

scope_limits: A single material-pending primary status is retained; this is not a completed naming-scope hold.
The upper route may involve the Remedios/Upipe tributary sequence, but the inspected regional prose is insufficient to assign that identity to selected parts.
An upper Hueque reservoir is documented regionally; no selected passage through it is established, and proposed reservoir descriptions are not treated as constructed features.
Final estuarine correspondence is regional and historical, without exact-bank, current-flow, tidal-condition or operational requirements.
No formal registry or whole-feature scalar name is verified.

records.region: Southeastern Labrador, western Alexis River headwaters through the Port Hope Simpson inner-estuary corridor.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity for the selected Alexis River drainage corridor. This includes its unnamed selected western feeder and the stored inner-estuary continuation associated with Alexis Bay; it does not assign the river hydronym to every waterbody or imply that the estuarine portion is freshwater river.
records.completion_scope: Complete ordinary geographic correspondence and supported representative system identity. Optional failed originals remain access-limited details; they do not erase the independent regional figure and station observations.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity for the selected Alexis River drainage corridor. This includes its unnamed selected western feeder and the stored inner-estuary continuation associated with Alexis Bay; it does not assign the river hydronym to every waterbody or imply that the estuarine portion is freshwater river.

scope_limits: The representative identity does not imply a single hydronym over every selected headward waterbody or the stored estuarine continuation.
Regional cartography generalizes minor channel bends and small islands. Correspondence is at ordinary corridor scale, without an exact bank or vertex requirement.
The names of individual western feeder reaches and small lakes are not established.
Formal registry records remain unverified; no CGN expanded/name-search evidence is used.

records.material_pending_reason: The chosen eastern headward branch and its complete approach into the independently sampled San Pedro/Cañar joining corridor remain unestablished. The middle and lower receiving valley, separate diversion setting and actual tidal-channel terminal are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Provisional receiving-river/system identity; San Pedro is a distinct bounded upper reach. No uniform name asserted for the whole selected route.
records.completion_scope: Bounded pass ended after two successful planning originals, one successful independent sampling thesis and two original-publication502 failures with the permitted identical retries. Further same-publication acquisition is paused; the remaining upper link is explicitly retained rather than inferred.
records.supported_name_scope: Provisional receiving-river/system identity; San Pedro is a distinct bounded upper reach. No uniform name asserted for the whole selected route.

scope_limits: The exact chosen upper opening and joining approach lack independent continuous geographic evidence.
Culebrillas and Silante names in broader planning prose do not identify the chosen opening and are not assigned to it.
No selected through-lake or reservoir passage is established; nearby named lakes and the separate diversion reservoir are not silently inserted into the route.
This is a source-material-pending result, not completed representative correspondence and not a completed whole-name scope hold.
Historical/compiled maps support ordinary corridors, not exact current banks, confluence vertices, hydraulic conditions or operations.

records.region: Southern Greenland: Inland Ice through the A. Kornerup Land and Holmlandet setting, continuing along the eastern side of Johan Dahl Land to the Narsarsuaq-side head of Tunulliarfik.
records.candidate_name_role: A. Kornerup Land, Holmlandet and Johan Dahl Land are exposed-land geography; Qooqqup Sermia is glacier geography; Qooroq and Tunulliarfik are fjord geography; Narsarsuaq is settlement geography. None supplies a whole-river candidate.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Actual retained originals expose the complete selected geography, but provide no representative natural-river hydronym or one surveyed continuous river through the interior ice, mixed Holmlandet passage and lower glacier/valley to the Narsarsuaq-side fjord head. No material geographic interval remains unread at ordinary source scale.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No representative whole-route natural-river identity established.
records.completion_scope: Complete ordinary regional and corridor-scale geographic correspondence of the chosen opening, every selected mainstem part and intermediate join, inland ice, exposed-rock and inland-pocket passage, lower glacier/valley/deposit sequence and actual terminal setting. This is not natural-river or hydraulic-continuity proof.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative whole-route natural-river identity established.

scope_limits: No representative whole-system natural-river name is established. Null does not demonstrate the absence of a local or official name.
Surface and subglacial continuity remain unverified.
Qooqqup Sermia and the nearby Qooroq fjord do not supply the identity of the full selected object; the actual ending is in the Narsarsuaq-side Tunulliarfik setting.
National ice-surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments are not river connectivity evidence.
Formal registry status and present physical drainage remain unverified.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
